title: Tale of the Merchant and His Wife

full_text:
The merchant who understood the language of animals lived happily in a countryside manor surrounded by gardens, flocks, and poultry. One starlit evening, as he sat upon the terrace beside his wife, a mother goat passed with her playful kid. The kid leaped into the air and tumbled into the irrigation channel. From the roost nearby, a venerable rooster crowed a witty observation to the farm dog about how young creatures test their boundaries before discovering their balance.

Hearing the bird's clever remark, the merchant could not restrain himself and burst into loud, merry laughter. His wife immediately turned to him with suspicious eyes and asked: "At what are you laughing with such delight? Are you mocking me in secret?"

The merchant smiled gently and placed his hand upon his chest. "By my honor, dear wife, my amusement was born of the barnyard banter which I alone can interpret. It touches you in no way whatsoever." Yet the wife, consumed by curiosity and wounded pride, refused to believe him. "You must tell me exactly what you heard," she insisted. "If you hide your secrets from me, it means your heart is no longer mine."

"Wife," pleaded the merchant, "I cannot disclose it! The covenant of my gift decrees that if I reveal what the beasts speak, my vitality and prosperity will perish." Still, she wept, locked herself in her chambers, and gathered her kinsmen, vowing to neither eat nor drink until the secret was laid bare. Torn between his love for her and the peril of his vow, the merchant sat in despair, preparing his will.

As he walked sorrowfully through the yard, he noticed the proud rooster strutting among the hens, pecking grains and crowing with supreme authority. The farm dog barked in annoyance: "How can you strut and rejoice when our master is preparing for his demise over his wife’s obstinacy?" The rooster shook his scarlet comb and answered: "Our master may be wise in languages, but he lacks resolve! A man must not surrender his life and judgment to petulant whim. A firm word, an unyielding boundary, and an olive branch of reason are the true remedies for domestic peace."

Hearing this, the merchant felt a veil lift from his eyes. He gathered his courage, entered his wife's presence with quiet authority, and told her plainly that her demands were unjust and that no whim would make him destroy their family. Seeing his unwavering resolve and dignity, the wife realized the folly of her relentless pressure. She cast aside her obstinacy, embraced him with newfound reverence, and domestic harmony returned to the manor forever.
moral: True household leadership requires firmness, calm discernment, and mutual respect, rather than yielding to endless unreasonable demands.
